For a magnetic field \vec{B}, parallel to Oz, with small values of m (orbital magnetic quantum number) and B=1T, compare the order of magnitude of the paramagnetic coupling term with transition energy \Delta E of Hydrogen atom with wavelength \lambda=0.4861\mu m.

PS: for the maths use an online LaTeX editor.

Choices:
A. \left\langle H\right\rangle =\Delta E
B. \left\langle H\right\rangle \ll\Delta E
C. \left\langle H\right\rangle \gg\Delta E
D. \left\langle H\right\rangle >\Delta E

Answer: <letter>

response.content:
The paramagnetic/Zeeman coupling for \(\vec B\parallel Oz\) is of order

\[
\left|\left\langle H\right\rangle\right|\sim \mu_B B |m|
\]

with \(\mu_B=9.27\times10^{-24}\,\mathrm{J/T}\). For \(B=1\,\mathrm T\),

\[
\mu_B B \approx 9.27\times10^{-24}\,\mathrm J
\approx 5.79\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{eV}.
\]

The transition wavelength is

\[
\lambda=0.4861\,\mu\mathrm m=486.1\,\mathrm{nm},
\]

so

\[
\Delta E=\frac{hc}{\lambda}\approx \frac{1240\,\mathrm{eV\,nm}}{486.1\,\mathrm{nm}}
\approx 2.55\,\mathrm{eV}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{|\langle H\rangle|}{\Delta E}\sim
\frac{5.79\times10^{-5}|m|}{2.55}\approx 2.3\times10^{-5}|m|\ll 1
\]

for small \(m\). Therefore the paramagnetic coupling is much smaller than the transition energy.

Answer: B
